The user just reported that a test run timed out immediately: the UI shows “Timed out after 0s (timeout)”. Looking back at the configuration I just applied to all agents, I see that I set `"timeoutSec": 0` in the adapter config for each Groq agent. In the Opencode adapter, a timeout value of 0 is interpreted as “no timeout” (i.e., infinite), but the Groq local adapter treats the literal 0 as an actual timeout duration of zero seconds, causing it to abort any request instantly. This explains the immediate timeout the user observed.

I need to communicate this discrepancy clearly to the user, pointing out that the `timeoutSec: 0` setting is the culprit. I should also hint that fixing it will involve changing the timeout to a positive number (or omitting it) so the Groq adapter behaves as intended. The user’s last message is just the timeout error, so a concise explanatory response is appropriate.

Thus I will respond with a short message that identifies the problem (`timeoutSec: 0`), explains the differing semantics between adapters, and notes that it needs fixing. This directly addresses the observed behavior and sets up the next step (adjusting the config).`timeoutSec: 0` — adapter take 0 literal, abort instant. Opencode treat 0 as "no timeout"; Groq adapter no. Fixing.
